text:
mona: FYI seeing a p99 token latency spike (~+450ms) on prod after the evicter/adaptive_v2 rollout at ~13:45 UTC. p50 fine. graphs show repeated microspikes aligned with eviction bursts. :eyes:

sam: which pool/region? any correlation with long-context requests?

mona: region eu-west-1, runtime pool runtime-1. spike correlates with a small set of long-context queries >28k tokens (LLM chat sessions).

taylor: saw a brief memory growth on ded-3 similar pattern last night. KV cache size climbs steadily and then a latency cliff when pager starts syncing.

raj: can you paste the evicter logs around the incident?

mona: pasted minimal log lines below (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T13:45:12Z] evicter.INFO reclaimed=0 pressure=high reuse_misses=0.87 queue_len=2048
[2026-03-17T13:45:12Z] evicter.DEBUG reinsert_slow_path=true held_ms=120
[2026-03-17T13:45:12Z] pager.WARN paging_start entries=512 write_batch=256
[2026-03-17T13:45:12Z] runtime.latency token_ms=450 evicter_blocked=true
```

sam: interesting that reclaimed=0 while queue_len is huge. suggests evicter scanning but failing to free entries (fragmentation?)

profile-bot: triggered collection: pprof mutex/profile for runtime-1 at 13:46Z. snippet: 

```
Mutex profile (30 samples):
  60.0% Evicter::reinsert_mutex
  20.0% Pager::write_lock
  10.0% KVMap::find_or_insert
  10.0% other
```

raj: that 60% in reinsert_mutex is a smoking gun. reinsert path should be mostly try_fast_reinsert w/o global lock. maybe adaptive_v2 flips algo and forces slow path under pressure.

taylor: we changed kernel selection and batching heuristics last week, which changed tokenization distribution -> more long sequential reads. could be a workload shift exposing a reinsert race or heavy lock hold.

sam: confirmed: when FIFO-mode engaged under adaptive_v2, we observed many reinserts for the same key sequences (reinsert thrash). FIFO increases churn on hotset edges, LRU would keep recent entries. if reinsert uses a global mutex, thrash -> head-of-line blocking -> latencies.

mona: quick repro steps I used: run loadtest with heavy long-context sessions (script attached), enable evicter.mode=adaptive_v2 and set evicter.paging_watermark=0.75. reproduce in ~60s.

mona: load command: `./tools/loadtest --profile long_context_heavy --rps 120 --seq-len 30k --duration 300`

raj: can someone run a flamegraph? I want to see whether kernel-selection change bumped a compiled path that increases per-token CPU and extends lock hold.

sam: I ran a flame for 30s during a spike: main hotspots in Evicter::reinsert and memcpy when paging. Not huge CPU, mostly blocked threads.

```
Flame (top):
 Evicter::reinsert -> evicter::evict_one -> pager::swap_out -> memcpy
 blocked threads: 45/128
```

joan: rolling a hotfix flag: disable `evicter.mode=adaptive_v2` for runtime-1 and runtime-2. will push in 2m.

deploy-bot: rollout started: disable-evicter-adaptive_v2 -> serverset=runtime-1, runtime-2 -> 8 nodes -> 2026-03-17T13:51:10Z

mona: after flag flip, p99 dropped back to baseline within ~30s. looks promising.

sam: can we avoid a full revert? short-term patch: reduce reinsert mutex scope + add per-vnode eviction quotas to avoid global thrash. also set evicter.max_evictions_per_tick=32 to spread work.

raj: agreed. probable root cause: policy crossover (LRU->FIFO heuristic) combined with reinsert slow path + global mutex -> eviction storms under long-context workload. the kernel/batching changes last week changed allocation patterns that exposed this.

taylor: I'll prepare a change that: 1) narrows reinsert lock, 2) tracks reinserts per-key per-tick to dedupe, 3) add metrics for reinserts/sec and reinsert_slow_path ratio.

joan: created ticket INF-1342 with rollback notes + telemetry task. linking traces and pprof.

mona: for postmortem: capture time-series of evicter.reclaimed, queue_len, reinsert_slow_path_pct, pager.write_latency, and token_p99 around the window. also correlate with kernel-selection rollout tags.

sam: one more note: we should test FIFO vs LRU in a synthetic harness that simulates 10% long-context heavy sessions and 90% short chats. the crossover point might be lower than we thought.

raj: thanks everyone. follow-up: taylor will open PR with lock-scope and metrics; sam will run synthetic compare harness; the flag remains off until we validate.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: disable-evicter-adaptive_v2 applied -> 2026-03-17T13:52:40Z

mona: p99 stable now. marking incident resolved for the moment. :white_check_mark:

profile-bot: archived pprof bundle: s3://redwood-profiles/pprof/1719991111-evicter-adaptive-v2-13-46.pbz

joan: will draft short blameless postmortem and add proposed infra tests.

sam: thanks, good catch. we should also add a canary that runs long-context workload when changing eviction policies.

mona: noted. will add to release checklist. :memo:
